theory: The supplied source supports estimating multiplication and division by rounding each number to one significant figure (question 12, lines 400–407). It does not teach the candidate's supplied-answer judgements, compatible-number checks, lower bounds or remainder critiques; the shared procedure and dependent examples must follow the supported method. Also, 'a misplaced digit usually makes an answer about ten times too big or small' is an unsupported generalisation: moving an individual digit need not scale the whole answer by ten.
summary: Replaced the unsupported practice and quiz tasks with question 12 estimation tasks, retaining calculation values, tiers and quiz ids while correcting structure slugs, answers and distractor explanations. reviewSummary: All practice items, quiz questions and worked examples use booklet-supported estimation types, and all supplied correct answers are mathematically correct. Repair two distractor explanations that confuse truncation with rounding; no whole-item removals or theory changes are needed.
